title: Fusing Two Randomized Trials under a Locally Misspecified Common Log-Odds Tilt
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field); fresh math and rubric panels pass with no findings; paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4 and salvageable=false.

proof_attempt_summary: The D-stage graph derived an all-procedure local Gaussian risk and connected-interval frontier for two binary randomized trials, including a paper-owned compact separation proof and observable Bernoulli transfer. After repairs to the full LAN score, isotropic reduction, and source positioning, fresh math and rubric panels passed with no findings. The general referee still assessed only subfield novelty against the field floor; a replayable finite certificate and validated application remain open, and no Lean formalization was started.
tldr: Two randomized trials can be fused under a common log-odds tilt with bounded Fisher-orthogonal local error.  The full product LAN contains outcome and covariate score coordinates for both sources; the external covariate coordinate is decision-ancillary and is quotiented without changing any decision value.  The resulting bounded Gaussian nuisance problem has an exact connected-action dual, convergent rational certificates, and uniform Bernoulli attainment.  The zero-radius and infinite-radius limits are exact-tilt and target-only inference, and external information strictly improves on target-only inference at every finite radius.  No fixed-refinement numerical value or strict published-rule comparison is claimed.
gap: Li et al. characterize exact-tilt efficiency and give an additive sensitivity interval, while Bonhomme--Weidner and Armstrong--Koles\'ar optimize regular or affine bias-aware procedures. None identifies the exact all-procedure risk or exact connected-interval expected-length value when the external randomized trial has a finite Fisher-orthogonal local tilt error.
fill: At each fixed baseline \(\gamma\), the project reduces the induced Bernoulli triangular arrays in \(\mathcal M_H(\gamma)\) to a bounded Gaussian nuisance experiment, proves when its perpendicular discrepancy is ancillary for the equivariant connected-endpoint problem, solves its minimax risk, poses and resolves the connected-interval dual, supplies certified convergent upper and lower programs, and transfers both values uniformly to implementable two-trial estimators and intervals.
